name: Unified Cybersecurity Platform
tag: Threat prevention, endpoint detection, admin access and patching in one console, with AI to sort what matters first.

scenarios.title: Suspicious activity on a laptop
scenarios.ask: One of our {endpoints} laptops started encrypting files in a shared folder. What's happening?
steps: Endpoint detection
Saw one process rename {=120 * response} files in 40 seconds on a finance laptop. Pattern matches ransomware behavior.
Responder
Applied your setting: {response}. The laptop was cut off from the network in under 10 seconds.
Hunter
Checked the other {=endpoints - 1} endpoints for the same file hash and process. None found.
Analyst
Traced the start to an email attachment opened 12 minutes earlier and blocked the sender.
followups: With alert only, the process keeps running until a person acts. Most teams allow isolation for this kind of pattern because seconds matter.
Can it isolate the wrong machine?
It can, rarely. Isolation is one click to undo, and every automatic action is logged with the reason.

scenarios.title: Patch backlog
scenarios.ask: We have {devices} devices and about {missing} critical patches missing on each. Our maintenance window is {window} on Sundays.
steps: Inventory
Found {=devices * missing} missing critical patches across {devices} devices.
Prioritizer
Put first the {=max(1, round(devices * 0.12))} internet-facing devices and any patch with a known exploit.
Scheduler
Each window can patch about {=window * 90} devices. Split the work into {=ceil(devices / (window * 90))} Sunday waves.
Verifier
After each wave, rescans and reports any device that failed to update.
followups: What if a patch breaks something?
Wave one goes to a small test group. If anything fails, later waves pause and you can roll that patch back.
Can we shorten the backlog faster?
Adding a second weekly window roughly halves the number of weeks. The planner shows both options.

scenarios.title: Admin access review
scenarios.ask: Review our {admins} admin accounts. Some haven't been checked in {days}.
steps: Access reader
Listed {admins} accounts with admin rights and their last sign-in.
Analyst
{=max(1, round(admins * 0.15))} accounts haven't signed in for 90 days. {=max(1, round(admins * 0.05))} belong to people who left.
Vault
Suggested moving shared admin passwords into the vault with check-out and auto-rotation.
Workflow
Sent each manager a list of their team's admin accounts to confirm or remove.
followups: Why is admin access such a risk?
Attackers who get an admin account can turn off defenses and reach everything. Fewer, monitored admin accounts shrink that risk.
Accounts are disabled first, not deleted, for 30 days. If a service needed one, it can be re-enabled quickly.
